dialect.detail: Explicitly states 'Enterprise COBOL v6.3 for z/OS' in the display output. Uses FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL and FUNCTION NUMVAL which are standard intrinsic functions. No EXEC CICS or EXEC SQL. Fixed format, no lines over 72 chars.
evidence: display 'in Enterprise COBOL v6.3 for z/OS'

purpose.domain_detail: Loan payment calculator computing monthly payment using the annuity formula A = P*(i*(1+i)^n)/((1+i)^n-1)
purpose.summary: An interactive console program that prompts the user for a loan principal, annual interest rate, and term in years, then calculates and displays the monthly payment and total cost of the loan using the standard annuity formula. It includes input validation for each parameter.

notable_features: FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL and FUNCTION NUMVAL for numeric input validation
Heavy use of GO TO for input validation loops (12 occurrences)
Exponentiation operator (**) for compound interest calculation
No PERFORM statements; control flow via GO TO only
No COMP-3 or packed decimal usage
verdict.notes: Program is clearly a student or educational exercise written by 'Clifford A. Chipman, EMIT' dated June 18, 2020. Targets IBM Enterprise COBOL v6.3 for z/OS but would likely compile on other COBOL-85 compliant compilers. The exclusive use of GO TO instead of PERFORM for looping is characteristic of a beginner or deliberately simplified style.
